# Footage from Google Flow is generated by the human, not by an API call

The bot's stock footage comes from Pexels, which is free and instant but
generic. Google's Veo produces something far better suited to a hook, and the
human running this bot has a Google AI Pro subscription — so the obvious move
is to have the bot generate the footage itself. It does not, and will not until
the numbers change.

Flow credits and Gemini API billing are separate systems: a Google AI Pro
subscription grants Flow credits inside the Flow app and no API access at all.
Generating from code means the paid Veo API, priced per second of output
(quoted August 2026: roughly $0.40/sec for Veo 3.1 Standard, from ~$0.03-0.05/sec
for Lite at 720p). A 45-second clip is five to seven cards, so an all-Veo clip
runs about $18 at Standard rates, and even Lite costs more per clip than Pexels
does per month. This bot makes one or two clips a day.

So the model call stays where the credits already are: the bot writes an
English Flow Prompt, the human pastes it into the Flow Android app, generates,
and replies to the prompt message in Telegram with the resulting mp4. The bot
files it against the Card that message belongs to and renders. Only the Hook
card takes this route — it is the one Card retention data says matters, and one
generation per clip fits inside the subscription with room to spare.

This follows the rule ADR 0001 set for uploads: anything that leaves the house,
costs money, or cannot be taken back stays behind a human press. The matching
is exact rather than inferred (a reply carries the message id; a filename or an
ordering guess does not), because footage silently attached to the wrong Card
produces a clip that renders cleanly and is about the wrong thing.

Reversing this means adding a Veo API client and a key — additive, and worth
revisiting if Lite pricing drops below what a clip is worth or if a Flow API
appears. The prices above were read from third-party summaries in August 2026;
check Google's own pricing page before acting on them.
